questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In a process, 701 J of heat is absorbed by a system and 394 J of work is done by the system. What is the change in internal energy (in J) for the process?
questions.solution:
Given, q = + 701 J (heat is absorbed, heance q is positive.)

W = - 394 J (work is done by the system, hence W is negative.)

By first law of thermodynamics;

Internal energy change, $\Delta \text{U} = \text{q} + \text{w}$
= + 701 J + (-394 J ) = + 307 J.

Hence, internal energy of the system increases by 307 J.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In which of the following conditions, a reaction will definitely be spontaneous:
questions.solution:
For a spontaneous reaction, $∆ G < 0.$

As per the Gibbs-Helmholtz equation,

$∆ G = ∆ H - T ∆ S$

When $∆ H$ is negative, i.e., the reaction is exothermic and $∆ S$ is positive, i.e., the disorder is increasing, the value of $∆ G$& will definitely be negative and the process will be spontaneous for all temperatures.

questions.q: In an isobaric process, when temperature changes from $T_1$ to $T_2, \Delta S$ is equal to
questions.solution:
The entropy change for a process, when $T$ and $P$ are the variables is given by
$\Delta S=C_P \ln \frac{T_2}{T_1}-R \ln \frac{P_2}{P_1}$
For an isobaric process $P_1=P_2$. Hence the above equation reduces to
$C_P \ln \frac{T_2}{T_1}=\Delta S$
or $\Delta S=2.303 C_P \log \frac{T_2}{T_1}$.

$\left({\text{K}}^{′} {\text{v}}^{2} = {\text{K}}^{′} \text{v} \text{v} = \text{P} \text{v} = \text{RT}\right)$

questions.q: At $25^{{}^{\circ}} \mathrm{C}$, when 1 mole of butane is heated, $\mathrm{CO}_2$ and liquid $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$ are formed, then the work done is
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{C}_4 \mathrm{H}_{10(g)}+\frac{13}{2} \mathrm{O}_{2(g)} \longrightarrow 4 \mathrm{CO}_{2(g)}+5 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_{(l)} \\ & \Delta n_g=4-\left(1+\frac{13}{2}\right)=-\frac{7}{2} \\ & w=-\Delta n_g R T=-\left(-\frac{7}{2} \times 0.0821 \times 298\right) \\ & =85.63 \mathrm{ L} \mathrm{ atm}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
A fixed mass $\text{m}$ of a gas is subjected to transformation of states from $\text{K}$ to $\text{L}$ to $\text{M}$ to $\text{N}$ and back to $\text{K}$ as shown in the figure.

The succeeding operation that enable this transformation of state are
questions.solution:
$K \to L$ : Isochoric process with increasing in pressure so by $\left(\dfrac{{T}_{L}}{{T}_{K}}\right) =\left(\dfrac{{P}_{L}}{{P}_{K}}\right)
${P}_{L} > {P}_{K}$ so ${T}_{L} > {T}_{K}$ so it is a case of heating
$L \to M: Isobaric process with increasing in $pressure so by \left(\dfrac{{T}_{M}}{{T}_{L}}\right) =\left(\dfrac{{V}_{M}}{{V}_{L}}\right)
${V}_{M} < {V}_{L}$ so ${T}_{M} < {T}_{L}$ so it is a case of cooling
Similarly for
$M \to N: Isochoric process with increasing in $pressure so by \left(\dfrac{{T}_{N}}{{T}_{M}}\right) =\left(\dfrac{{P}_{N}}{{P}_{M}}\right)
${P}_{N} < {P}_{M}$ so ${T}_{N} < {T}_{M}$ so it is a case of cooling$
